ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r15.claim: He cites a Prophetic hadith teaching that anything which hurts a believer is a calamity for that believer.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r15.anchor: hadîs-i şerîfi mûcebince ezâ verecek herhangi bir zarara giriftâr oldukları zaman

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r16.claim: When any harmful loss befalls them, the patient say the formula of belonging to God and returning to Him, finding comfort through submission.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r16.anchor: Allah’a arz-ı teslîmiyet ile mütesellî olarak sabrederler

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r17.claim: They say this not only with their tongues but wholeheartedly, reflecting on the purpose of creation.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r17.anchor: bunu yalnız lisânen değil, gāye-i halk u hilkati düşünerek bütün kalb ile söylerler.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r18.claim: Saying that they belong to God acknowledges that all property and selves belong to Him and that His will over them cannot rightly be challenged; this is acceptance of divine decree and the station of the contented soul.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r18.anchor: emvâl ü enfüs her şeyi Allah’a teslim ve Allah teâlâ’nın milki olan her şeyde

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r19.claim: Saying that they return to God affirms death and eventual return, while hoping for divine acceptance and union rather than absolute nonbeing; this is the station of the soul pleasing to God.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r19.anchor: gayenin ‘adem-i mutlak olmayıp visâl-i küllî olduğuna iman ve bu iman ile ‘indallah marzî olmak ümidini izhar vardır

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r20.claim: Through religious knowledge and Prophetic ethics the soul rises through five stages: commanding, self-reproaching, tranquil, content, and pleasing to God.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r20.anchor: İnsanın nefsi ibtidâ nefs-i emmâre iken ma‘ârif-i dîniye ve ahlâk-ı Muhammediye ile terakki ederek sâniyen nefs-i levvâme

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r21.claim: The divine address in al-Fajr describes the contented and divinely approved soul returning to its Lord.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r22.claim: Return to God is not movement toward a place or direction, since God is transcendent beyond both.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r22.anchor: Bu rücû‘un bir mekân ve cihete intikal suretiyle olmadığı âşikârdır. Zira Allah teâlâ cihet ü mekândan münezzehtir

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r23.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r23.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r23.claim: He presents three possible senses of return: a figurative confession of annihilation, a confession of subsistence, or an acknowledgment of both in different respects.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r23.anchor: 1. Bu, nefsimiz hakkında bir ikrâr-ı fenâdan kinayedir. 2. İkrâr-ı bekādır. 3. Min vechin fenâ ve min vechin bekāyı ikrardır.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r24.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r24.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r24.claim: He chooses the third sense: affirming our essential passing away and our subsistence only through God.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r24.anchor: Bizce doğrusu bu üçüncüsüdür. Zira hepimizin fenâ-yı zâtîsi ile bekā-billâhı ikrardır.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r25.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r25.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r25.claim: As at our origin, after death we will exist only in divine knowledge and decree, not through existence that is our own.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r25.anchor: yine onun gibi yok olacağız ve olduğumuz gibi yalnız ilm-i ilâhîde ve sırf hükm-i ilâhîde mevcud kalacağız

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r26.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r26.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r26.claim: People are born with their innate endowments before acting, but die carrying what they have earned, good or bad, and bearing responsibility.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r26.anchor: giderken ise iyi veya kötü kazanacağımızı kazanmış, iyilik veya kötülük nâmına neyimiz varsa hepsini omuzumuza almış, mes’ûliyeti yüklenmiş olarak gideceğiz.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r27.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r27.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r27.claim: Our essence rests on divine knowledge, existence on God’s existence, and continuance on divine subsistence; return means enduring through God in a manifestation of beauty or majesty.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#2/r27.anchor: zâtımız ilm-i ilâhî ile, vücûdumuz vücûd-i ilâhî ile, bekāmız da bekā-yı ilâhî ile kāim olur.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r1.speaker: Râzî
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r1.claim: Razi reads the return as referring to the hereafter: in this world people appear to control benefits and harms, but after death only God’s judgment governs them.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r1.anchor: Râzî diyor ki “Bu rücû‘âhirete işârettir. Biz dünyada iken az çok kendimiz veya başkaları da menfaat ve mazarratımıza zâhiren mâlik bulunuyorduk

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r2.claim: This return entails resurrection, gathering, and other afterlife judgments through a new creation; the true hereafter is the eternal life after resurrection.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r2.anchor: halk-ı cedîd ile ba‘s, haşr ü neşr ve sâir ahkâm-ı uhreviye terettüb edebilecektir. Ve asıl âhiret ba‘sten sonraki hayât-ı ebediye olacaktır.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r3.claim: The return in this verse also covers the interval after death and before resurrection, which some explain as the soul’s continued existence.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r3.anchor: buradaki rücû‘mevtten sonra ve ba‘sten evvelki hâlete de şâmildir, buna bazıları “bekā-yı rûh” nâmını vermiş

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r4.claim: The phrase “soul’s continued existence” suggests self-subsistence, while return to God entails acknowledging essential annihilation and therefore means more than that.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r4.anchor: “bekā-yı rûh” tâbirinde bir bekā-yı zâtî şâibesi vardır, rücû‘da ise fenâ-yı zâtîyi itiraf münderictir.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r5.claim: Though the body perishes and the soul may persist for a time, at the great Resurrection even souls may perish; 28:88 states that all perishes except God’s Face, while the reality known to God is never lost and can be recreated.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r5.anchor: zâtîmiz ez-her cihet tahakkuk edeceği ve ancak

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r6.claim: Whether the reality known to God is soul, body, both, or something beyond them, any continued existence is possible only through divine subsistence, not as our own independent survival.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r6.anchor: eğer bunların mâverâsında bir şey ise o suretle bir bekāya nâil olacağımız ve bu bekā hakikaten bizim kendi kendimize bir bekāmız demek olmayıp ancak bekā-yı ilâhî ile mümkin olan bir bekāmız olacaktır.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r7.claim: Our natural condition is mortality; our ultimate destiny is to endure through God in a manifestation of majesty or beauty, with eternal divine beauty as the highest aim.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r7.anchor: bizim tabîî denebilecek muktezâ-yı zâtımız fânîlik iken mukadderâtımız, nasîbimiz, bekā-billâh tarîkiyle mazhar-ı celâl veya cemâl olmaktır

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r8.claim: He says the scientific law of the persistence of cause supports this meaning: effects and partial forces vanish, while God alone, the universal cause, remains and their individual identities are preserved in divine knowledge.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r8.anchor: Fennin bekā-yı illet kānûn-ı azîminde bu mâna sâbit demektir. Maddeler, cüz’î kuvvetler hepsi ma‘luldürler

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r9.claim: Philosophers who use “spiritual subsistence” treat the human soul as though it shared divine reality and make soul survival the basis of the hereafter, thereby confusing the truth.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r9.anchor: bu vechile bekā-billâha “bekā-yı rûhânî” tâbirini kullanan feylesoflar hakīkat-i ilâhiyeyi rûh ve rûh-i beşeri hakīkat-i ilâhiyeden gibi düşündüklerinden dolayı

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r10.claim: The soul is a mystery belonging to God’s command and its survival is possible, but making our own eternal survival the basis of the hereafter assigns us self-subsistence and forgets God as First Cause.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r10.anchor: Rûh gerçi emr-i Rab olan bir sırdır. Ve bekā-yı rûh bir emr-i münker de değildir. Fakat bizim ebediyen bekā-yı rûhumuzla bekāmıza hükmetmek bize bir bekā-yı zâtî isnad eylemektir.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r11.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r11.claim: The Real is beyond spiritual and corporeal reality in a level of unity; the Lord governs the spirit that belongs to His command.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r11.anchor: hakīkat-i hak rûhâniyet ve cismâniyetin fevkinde bir mertebe-i ehadiyyettedir. Rûh emr-i Rab olmakla beraber, Rab emrine hâkimdir.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r12.claim: The reminder that God prevails over His command (12:21) must not be forgotten.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r12.anchor: Rûh emr-i Rab olmakla beraber, Rab emrine hâkimdir.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r13.claim: God is the source and foundation of our existence and subsistence; He alone is the Living and Sustainer, and we endure through Him.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r13.anchor: bizim vücûd ve bekāmızın merci‘ü mebnâsı Allah’ın vücûd ve bekāsıdır. Biz kendi bekāmızla değil, Allah’ın bekāsıyla bâkī olabileceğiz, Hayy ü Kayyûm odur.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r14.claim: The formula “We belong to God and return to Him” expresses subsistence through God.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r14.anchor: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّآ إِلَيْهِ رَٰجِعُونَ işte bu bekā-billâhı nâtıktır.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r15.claim: This is neither solely spiritual nor solely bodily survival, but the real subsistence that grounds both; the hereafter rests on it.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r16.claim: As long as God exists and endures, renewed spiritual and bodily forms remain endlessly possible.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r16.anchor: Allah mevcud ve bâkī oldukça bizim için yeniden yeniye nice nice rûhâniyetlere, cismâniyetlere mazhariyet dâima mümkin ve nâmütenâhî münkindir.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r17.claim: After death the soul may remain and be rewarded or punished in the grave and barzakh, or may itself perish later; no one can escape divine knowledge or subsistence through God, the basis of reward and punishment.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r17.anchor: âlem-i kabr ve berzahta müsâb ve mu‘âteb olabilir, kalmaması ve bir müddet sonra onun da fenâya gitmesi nefsinde mümkindir.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r18.claim: The hereafter is not merely survival of the soul: after barzakh there is resurrection in a distinct new creation, whose purpose is return to God in that new state.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r18.anchor: âhiret sadece bir bekā-yı rûh olmayıp hayât-ı berzahiyeden sonra başkaca bir neş’et ile ba‘s olacak

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r19.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r19.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r19.claim: The formula asserts both a return that guarantees the hereafter and a further return in the hereafter as the highest aim and perfection.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r19.anchor: bir taraftan damân-ı âhiret olan bir rücû‘u, bir taraftan da âhirette dahi aksâ-yı emel ve gāye-i kemâl olan bir rücû‘u

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r20.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r20.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r20.claim: Hope and fear based on subsistence through God are higher, truer, and more scientific than those based only on the theory of the soul’s survival.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r20.anchor: bekā-billâh ile ümîd ü mehâfet sadece bekā-yı rûh nazariyesine müesses ümîd ü mehâfetten çok yüksek, çok hakīkī, çok ilmîdir.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r21.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r21.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r21.claim: This is pure tawhid and Islam directed to God; the surah of Joseph will show that this consolation was not given to communities other than Muhammad’s.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r21.anchor: Her şâibeden müberrâ bir tevhid, bir İslâm ilallah’tır. Ve Sûre-i Yûsuf’da geleceği üzere bu tesliyet ümmet-i Muhammed’den başkasına verilmemiştir.

ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r22.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r22.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r22.claim: Those who rely all their hope on subsistence through God and reach the contented and approved stations deserve every glad tiding.
ELMALILI:2:153-157#3/r22.anchor: bütün ümidini bekā-billâha istinad ettirerek râziye ve marziye makamlarına ermiş olan sâbirler her müjdeye lâyıktırlar.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r2.claim: Alladhīna may be an accusative adjective for al-ṣābirīn, an accusative phrase of praise, or nominative with an implied subject as detachment or resumption; it may also be a topic with أولئك as predicate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r2.anchor: يجوز في الذين أن يكون منصوبا على النعت للصابرين، وهو ظاهر الإعراب، أو منصوبا على المدح

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r3.claim: Muṣība is an active participle of aṣābat, specialized for an unpleasant event and used like a noun that accepts syntactic governance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r3.anchor: مصيبة: اسم فاعل من أصابت، وصار لها اختصاص بالشيء المكروه، وصارت كناية عن الداهية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r4.claim: The pairing aṣābat-hum muṣība is paronomasia between a verb and noun, like 53:57 and 56:1.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r4.anchor: وأصابتهم مصيبة: من التجنيس المغاير، وهو أن يكون إحدى الكلمتين اسما والأخرى فعلا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r5.claim: Any harm to a believer's self, property, or family counts as a calamity, however small; a Prophetic report says he performed istirjāʿ when his lamp went out.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r5.anchor: والمصيبة: كل ما أذى المؤمن في نفس أو مال أو أهل، صغرت أو كبرت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r6.claim: The Prophet is reported to have said istirjāʿ when a lamp he needed went out, treating this as a calamity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r6.anchor: وروي ذلك عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، أنه استرجع عند انطفاء مصباحه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r7.claim: The particle idhā here indicates repeated, general occurrence; grammarians disagree whether idhā denotes repetition or only one instance.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r7.anchor: والمعنى في إذا هنا: على التكرار والعموم. وقد تقدم لنا ذكر الخلاف في إذا، أتدل على التكرار

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r8.claim: Qālū innā lillāh is the response to idhā within the relative clause; innā contracts from innanā by dropping the second nūn to avoid identical sounds, so it remains governing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r8.anchor: قالوا إنا لله: قالوا: جواب إذا، والشرط وجوابه صلة للذين. وإنا: أصله إننا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r9.claim: Saying lillāh acknowledges God's ownership and our servitude, affirming that He directs us in whatever matters He wills.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p56/r9.anchor: ولله: معناه الإقرار بالملك والعبودية لله، فهو المتصرف فينا بما يريد من الأمور

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r1.claim: The return to God affirms resurrection, recalls death as the greatest calamity, and teaches that lesser losses should be easier to bear patiently.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r1.anchor: وإنا إليه راجعون: إقرار بالبعث وتنبيه على مصيبة الموت التي هي أعظم المصائب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r2.claim: One interpretation says our souls, possessions, and families belong to God, who does not wrong us in what He does.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r2.anchor: نفوسنا وأموالنا وأهلينا لله لا يظلمنا فيما يصنعه بنا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r3.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r3.claim: Another interpretation says the words surrender affairs to God and accept His decree; returning means resurrection for reward or punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r3.anchor: أسلمنا الأمر لله ورضينا بقضائه، وإنا إليه راجعون يعني: للبعث لثواب المحسن ومعاقبة المسيء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r4.claim: A third interpretation takes returning to God as returning to Him for compensation of the loss and abundant reward.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r4.anchor: راجعون إليه في جبر المصاب وإجزال الثواب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r5.claim: A further explanation reads the first clause as acknowledging God's dominion and the second as acknowledging annihilation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r5.anchor: إقرار بالمملكة في قوله: إنا لله، وإقرار بالهلكة في قوله: وإنا إليه راجعون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r6.speaker: المنتخب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r6.claim: Al-Muntakhab explains that attributing the event to a calamity rather than God includes both divine and human causes: in the first case surrender to God's rule, in the second seek justice from Him without transgressing.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r6.anchor: أن إسناد الإصابة إلى المصيبة، لا إلى الله تعالى، ليعم ما كان من الله، وما كان من غيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r7.claim: Another view says innā lillāh expresses present acceptance of what happened, while innā ilayhi rājiʿūn expresses acceptance of whatever will happen later.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r7.anchor: وقيل: إنا لله، دليل على الرضا بما نزل به في الحال، وإنا إليه راجعون، دليل على الرضا في الحال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r8.claim: The verse contains an obligation to submit to God's command and decree and patiently perform duties, plus a voluntary act of voicing istirjāʿ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r8.anchor: واشتملت الآية على فرض ونفل. فالفرض: التسليم لأمر الله، والرضا بقدره، والصبر على أداء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r9.claim: Voicing istirjāʿ has benefits, including angering disbelievers by displaying seriousness in obedience to God's commands and avoidance of prohibitions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p57/r9.anchor: وفي إظهاره فوائد منها: غيظ الكفار لعلمهم بجده في طاعة الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p60/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p60/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p60/r10.claim: The Prophet is to give glad tidings to Muslims who patiently accept God's decree in belief and speech, confessing that they are God's servants and return to Him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p60/r10.anchor: ثم أمر نبيه أن يبشر الصابرين على ما ابتلوا به المسلمين لقضاء الله اعتقادا وقولا صريحا أنهم عبيد الله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r6.claim: The words of return are a refuge and protection for the afflicted because they affirm God's oneness, servitude, resurrection, and certainty that all affairs return to Him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r6.anchor: وجعل هذه الكلمات ملجأ لذوي المصائب وعصمة للممتحنين لما جمعت من المعاني المباركة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r7.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r7.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says no prophet before Muḥammad received these words; had Jacob known them, he would not have lamented Joseph.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r7.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: لم يعط هذه الكلمات نبي قبل نبينا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r8.claim: A report says the Prophet's lamp went out at night and he recited the words of return; when asked whether this was a calamity, he said anything that harms a believer is one.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p227#2/r8.anchor: فقال: «نعم كل ما آذى المؤمن فهي مصيبة»

NAHHAS:v1p272/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p272/r4.speaker: الكسائي
NAHHAS:v1p272/r4.claim: He allows the alif in إنا لله to be imāla toward kasra because the expression is frequent.
NAHHAS:v1p272/r4.anchor: قال الكسائي إن شئت كسرت الألف لاستعمالها وكثرتها

NAHHAS:v1p272/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p272/r5.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v1p272/r5.claim: He attributes the kasra in the expression to frequent usage; Nahhas calls this badly mistaken because nūn is not kasra and an alif cannot be vowelled.
NAHHAS:v1p272/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء وإنما كسرت النون في إنا لله لكثرة استعمالهم إياها

NAHHAS:v1p272/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p272/r6.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p272/r6.claim: The alif is inclined toward kasra because of لله; frequent use makes the words act as one, unlike إنا لزيد.
NAHHAS:v1p272/r6.anchor: وإنما أميلت الألف في إنا لله لكسرة اللام في لله ولو قلت إنا لزيد

NAHHAS:v1p272/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p272/r7.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p272/r7.claim: The alif may instead receive full tafkhīm; the underlying إننا loses one nūn for lightness, as in وإنا إليه راجعون.
NAHHAS:v1p272/r7.anchor: وإن شئت فخمت والأصل إننا حذفت إحدى النونين تخفيفا وكذا ( وإنا إليه راجعون )

MUQATIL:2:153-157/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:153-157/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:153-157/r5.claim: Those afflicted respond that they belong to God and return to Him; the Lord's prayers mean forgiveness, as in 9:103, where praying upon people means seeking forgiveness and the prayer is a supplication that comforts them.
MUQATIL:2:153-157/r5.anchor: يعنى مغفرة، كقوله سبحانه: وصل عليهم يعنى استغفر لهم

TABATABAI:2:153-157/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r1.claim: These five verses form one tightly connected unit whose opening leads to its ending and whose ending returns to its opening, so they were revealed together.
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r1.anchor: بيان خمس آيات متحدة السياق، متسقة الجمل، ملتئمة المعاني، يسوق أولها إلى آخرها ويرجع آخرها إلى أولها

TABATABAI:2:153-157/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r2.claim: Their context places them just before fighting and jihad are legislated, warning believers of a public trial soon to come.
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r2.anchor: وسياقها ينادي بأنها نزلت قبيل الأمر بالقتال وتشريع حكم الجهاد، ففيه ذكر من بلاء سيقبل على المؤمنين

TABATABAI:2:153-157/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r3.claim: Individual hardship is severe but other people can support the sufferer; collective calamity disables shared judgment and planning, compounding fear and weakening resolve.
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r3.anchor: والبلاء الفردي وإن كان شاقا على الشخص المبتلى بذلك، مكروها، لكن ليس مهولا مهيبا

TABATABAI:2:153-157/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r4.claim: The coming trial is not ordinary plague or famine but conflict provoked by the believers' monotheism; opponents exhausted other means, leaving fighting as the remaining instrument.
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r4.anchor: ولا كل بلاء عام كالوباء والقحط بل بلاء عام قربتهم منها أنفسهم، فإنهم أخذوا دين التوحيد

TABATABAI:2:153-157/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r5.claim: Both the enemies' suppression of truth and the believers' removal of falsehood now require force, since argument and other approaches no longer work.
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r5.anchor: ولا وسيلة تحسم مادة النزاع وتقطع الخلاف غير القتال، فسائر الوسائل كإقامة الحجة وبث الفتنة

TABATABAI:2:153-157/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r6.claim: The verses urge believers to face battle by portraying death in God's path as life, and teach patience and prayer as protection from panic and reliance on God.
TABATABAI:2:153-157/r6.anchor: فالآيات تستنهض المؤمنين على القتل، وتخبرهم أن أمامهم بلاء ومحنة

TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r2.claim: Steadfast people are those who say the return formula when struck by an unpleasant calamity; it must express a real awareness, not empty speech or passing thought.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r2.anchor: وهي الواقعة التي تصيب الإنسان، ولا يستعمل لفظ المصيبة إلا في النازلة المكروهة

TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r3.claim: True patience comes from realizing that one's whole being belongs to God and returns to Him, cutting off the roots of panic, grief, and heedlessness.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r3.anchor: وهي ان الإنسان مملوك لله بحقيقة الملك، وان مرجعه إلى الله سبحانه وبه يتحقق أحسن الصبر

TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r4.claim: Every human existence, faculty, and action depends on God; a person has no independent ownership, while any apparent possession exists only by divine permission.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#6/r4.anchor: بيانه أن وجود الإنسان وجميع ما يتبع وجوده من قواه وأفعاله، قائم الذات بالله الذي هو فاطره وموجده

TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r1.claim: God alone truly owns everything; human ownership of self, children, and wealth is only apparent and will end, so a believer should not grieve as though something were truly lost.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r1.anchor: فإذا تذكر الإنسان حقيقة ملكه تعالى، ونسبه إلى نفسه فوجد نفسه ملكا طلقا لربه

TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r2.claim: Moral traits are formed by repeatedly practicing fitting actions until their effects become stable dispositions; repeated courage in danger can overcome cowardice.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r2.anchor: إنما هو بتكرار الأعمال الصالحة المناسبة لها ومزاولتها، والمداومة عليها، حتى تثبت في النفس

TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r3.claim: The first ethical method motivates virtues by worldly outcomes and public approval: restraint brings esteem, greed brings poverty or humiliation, while learning, courage, and justice yield respect and ease.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r3.anchor: المسلك الأول تهذيبها بالغايات الصالحة الدنيوية، والعلوم والآراء المحمودة عند الناس

TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r4.claim: This is the familiar method of ancient Greek and other ethical writers, but the Quran does not base moral choice on what society praises or condemns.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#7/r4.anchor: وهذا هو المسلك المعهود الذي رتب عليه علم الأخلاق، والمأثور من بحث الأقدمين من يونان وغيرهم فيه

TABATABAI:2:153-157#8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#8/r4.claim: A second ethical path motivates conduct by afterlife reward and punishment, a method frequently used in the Quran, including promised paradise, measureless reward, and painful punishment.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#8/r4.anchor: المسلك الثاني الغايات الأخروية، وقد كثر ذكرها في كلامه تعالى كقوله سبحانه إن الله اشترى من المؤمنين أنفسهم وأموالهم

TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r1.claim: Every society must value giving each person their due, proportionate pursuit and defense of benefits, and knowledge that distinguishes human benefit; these are justice, temperance, courage, and wisdom.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r1.anchor: وهذه هي العدالة والعفة، والشجاعة، والحكمة التي ذكرنا أن الاجتماع الإنساني كيفما فرض لا يحكم إلا بحسنها

TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r2.claim: Modesty against disgrace is a branch of temperance; indignation when sanctities and rights are violated is courage; contentment and humility also belong among social virtues.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r2.anchor: وهو الحياء من شعب العفة أو لا يحكم بوجوب السخط وتغير النفس في هتك المقدسات وهضم الحقوق، وهو الغيرة من شعب الشجاعة

TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r3.claim: Apparent disagreements among societies over virtue arise from disagreement about whether particular cases instantiate a virtue, not from disagreement about the general moral rule.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r3.anchor: بل من جهة الاختلاف في انطباق الحكم على المصداق وعدم انطباقه

TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r4.claim: Autocratic societies treated a king's unrestricted power as a legitimate royal right, so they did not classify it as injustice under their own understanding.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r4.anchor: كانت ترى لعرش الملك الاختيار التام في أن يفعل ما يشاء، ويحكم ما يريد

TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r5.claim: Medieval France reportedly treated learning as discreditable for kings because it seemed incompatible with political and governmental duties, not because knowledge was despised as a virtue.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r5.anchor: كما يحكى عن ملة فرنسا في القرون الوسطى، ولم يكن ذلك لتحقيرهم فضيلة العلم

TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r6.claim: Societies that seem to reject women's chastity, modesty, men's protective jealousy, contentment, or humility do so because they classify those cases differently, not because they deny the virtues themselves.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r6.anchor: لا لأن هذه الفضائل ليست فضائل عندهم

TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r7.claim: Their continued praise of a ruler's and judge's justice, law-abiding modesty, defense of independence and sacred things, contentment with legal rights, and deference to guides shows that the underlying virtues remain valued.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#27/r7.anchor: يمدحون عفة الحاكم في حكمه والقاضي في قضائه، ويمدحون الاستحياء من مخالفة القوانين

TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r1.claim: The claim that morals are good only when they serve a social goal equivocates between an actual natural social order and a hypothetical plan imposed on people; their judgments are not interchangeable.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r1.anchor: فإن المراد بالاجتماع الهيئة الحاصلة من عمل مجموع القوانين التي قررتها الطبيعة بين الأفراد المجتمعين

TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r2.claim: Even if natural society itself were thought to make no moral judgments, a plan suited to human happiness would still ultimately depend on stable human nature.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r2.anchor: وأنها تنتهي بالآخرة إلى اقتضاء مستمر من الطبيعة

TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r3.claim: If moral rules followed each plan, contradictory social aims would destroy shared reasoning and leave force in control, contradicting nature's purpose in bringing humans into society.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#28/r3.anchor: أدى ذلك إلى ارتفاع الحجة المشتركة المقبولة عند عامة الاجتماعات، ولم يكن التقدم والنجاح حينئذ إلا للقدرة والتحكم

TABATABAI:2:153-157#29/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#29/r8.speaker: أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:153-157#29/r8.claim: Ali explains that saying we belong to God acknowledges His ownership, while saying we return to Him acknowledges our annihilation; al-Tabataba'i says the meaning was already clarified and notes a fuller al-Kafi version.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#29/r8.anchor: عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام قال - وقد سمع رجلا يقول إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون - يا هذا إن قولنا إنا لله إقرار منا بالملك

TABATABAI:2:153-157#29/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#29/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:153-157#29/r9.claim: Al-Tabataba'i says the meaning of Ali's saying follows from his earlier discussion and notes that al-Kafi transmits it in fuller form.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#29/r9.anchor: وقد اتضح معناه بما تقدم ورواه في الكافي مفصلا

TABATABAI:2:153-157#30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#30/r1.speaker: الله عز وجل
TABATABAI:2:153-157#30/r1.claim: The Prophet reports God as saying that what people give up for Him earns tenfold to seven hundredfold, while those deprived by force receive three gifts that would satisfy even angels.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#30/r1.anchor: قال الله عز وجل إني جعلت الدنيا بين عبادي قرضا فمن أقرضني فيها قرضا أعطيته بكل واحدة عشرا

TABATABAI:2:153-157#30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:153-157#30/r2.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:153-157#30/r2.claim: Al-Sadiq identifies the three gifts for a person whose property God takes by force as divine blessings, mercy, and guidance, relating them to the verse about those who say they belong to God and return to Him.
TABATABAI:2:153-157#30/r2.anchor: ثم قال أبو عبد الله قول الله { الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون أولئك عليهم صلوات من ربهم }

STUDYQURAN:2:156/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r1.claim: Most Muslims traditionally recite this phrase when they learn of another person's death.
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r1.anchor: Truly we are God’s, and unto Him we return, traditionally recited by most Muslims at the moment of learning of another’s death

STUDYQURAN:2:156/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r2.claim: The formula connects with the loss of souls mentioned in the preceding verse.
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r2.anchor: is connected with the loss of souls mentioned in the previous verse.

STUDYQURAN:2:156/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r3.claim: Return to God is a recurring Quranic theme: all matters return to Him, people are warned of their return on the Day, and they return willingly or unwillingly and all together.
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r3.anchor: human beings often are reminded that unto God are all matters returned (2:210) and are warned to be mindful of a day when they shall be returned to God (2:281), willingly or unwillingly (3:83), all together (5:48).

STUDYQURAN:2:156/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r4.claim: Humanity's belonging to God extends Quranic statements that everything in the heavens and earth belongs to Him.
STUDYQURAN:2:156/r4.anchor: That human beings belong to God is an extension of such passages as Unto Him belongs whatsoever is in the heavens and on the earth (v. 116; see also vv. 255, 284)

TAB-FULL:v2p706/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p706/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p706/r1.claim: The patient recognize every blessing as God's, affirm their servitude and His sole lordship, believe in returning to Him, submit to His trials and judgments, and hope for reward while fearing punishment.
TAB-FULL:v2p706/r1.anchor: إنا مماليك ربنا ومعبودنا أحياء ونحن عبيده

TABATABAI:2:155-156/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:155-156/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:155-156/r6.claim: The repeated mention of the patient announces their reward, teaches beautiful patience, grounds it in God's ownership of people, and states its general reward: blessing, mercy, and guidance.
TABATABAI:2:155-156/r6.anchor: أعاد ذكر الصابرين ليبشرهم أولا، ويبين كيفية الصبر بتعليم ما هو الصبر الجميل ثانيا، ويظهر به حق الأمر

TABATABAI:2:155-156#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:155-156#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:155-156#2/r1.claim: These verses teach a distinctive divine knowledge with real effects, unlike philosophers' ethical training based on social judgments or prophetic legal training based on duties and recompense; this third path is complete pure monotheism.
TABATABAI:2:155-156#2/r1.anchor: فإن هذه الآيات وأمثالها مشتملة على معارف خاصة إلهية ذات نتائج خاصة حقيقية لا تشابه تربيتها نوع التربية

TABRISI:2:156-157/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r1.speaker: الكسائي
TABRISI:2:156-157/r1.claim: In some transmissions, al-Kisāʾī applies imāla to the nūn in innā and the lām in lillāh; other readers pronounce them with tafkhīm.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r1.anchor: أمال الكسائي في بعض الروايات النون من إنا واللام من لله والباقون بالتفخيم

TABRISI:2:156-157/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:156-157/r2.claim: Imāla is allowed in innā with God's name because of the kasra and frequent use, which make the sequence almost one word.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r2.anchor: وإنما جازت الإمالة في هذه الألف مع اسم الله للكسرة مع كثرة الاستعمال حتى صارت بمنزلة الكلمة الواحدة

TABRISI:2:156-157/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r3.speaker: الفراء
TABRISI:2:156-157/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says innā cannot be imāla before a name other than Allah, since particles and similar forms normally resist imāla and inflection like parts of a word.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r3.anchor: قال الفراء: لا يجوز إمالة إنا مع غير الاسم الله تعالى

TABRISI:2:156-157/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:156-157/r4.claim: Muṣība is a hardship that strikes the soul through the harm it causes; its name derives from striking or befalling someone with a calamity.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r4.anchor: المصيبة المشقة الداخلة على النفس لما يلحقها من المضرة وهو من الإصابة كأنها تصيبها بالنكبة

TABRISI:2:156-157/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:156-157/r5.claim: Returning is a thing's return to a prior state, as in a house becoming someone's property again; it is synonymous with returning and becoming.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r5.anchor: والرجوع مصير الشيء إلى ما كان يقال رجعت الدار إلى فلان إذا ملكها مرة ثانية وهو نظير العود والمصير

TABRISI:2:156-157/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:156-157/r6.claim: Guidance means attaining the path of truth.

TABRISI:2:156-157/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:156-157/r7.claim: The verse describes patient people who, when struck by a personal or financial calamity, prepare themselves to bear it in hope of reward.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r7.anchor: أي نالتهم نكبة في النفس أو المال فوطنوا أنفسهم على ذلك احتسابا للأجر

TABRISI:2:156-157/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:156-157/r8.claim: Saying we belong to God is an acknowledgment of servitude: we are His servants and property.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r8.anchor: هذا إقرار بالعبودية أي نحن عبيد الله وملكه

TABRISI:2:156-157/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:156-157/r9.claim: Saying we return to God is an acknowledgment of resurrection and the final return to His judgment.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r9.anchor: هذا إقرار بالبعث والنشور أي نحن إلى حكمه نصير

TABRISI:2:156-157/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r10.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:2:156-157/r10.claim: The Commander of the Faithful says the first phrase acknowledges God's ownership of us and the second acknowledges our perishing.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r10.anchor: ولهذا قال أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام: إن قولنا إنا لله إقرار على أنفسنا بالملك

TABRISI:2:156-157/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:156-157/r11.claim: The formula consoles because God will repair a justly incurred calamity and secure justice against its perpetrator if it was unjust; it expresses submission to His plan and trust in His judgment.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r11.anchor: وإنما كانت هذه اللفظة تعزية عن المصيبة لما فيها من الدلالة على أن الله تعالى يجبرها

TABRISI:2:156-157/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r12.speaker: الحديث
TABRISI:2:156-157/r12.claim: A hadith says that whoever says istirjāʿ when struck by calamity will have God repair the affliction, improve the outcome, and grant a pleasing righteous replacement.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r12.anchor: من استرجع عند المصيبة جبر الله مصيبته

TABRISI:2:156-157/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157/r13.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
TABRISI:2:156-157/r13.claim: The Commander of the Faithful says that even if much time has passed, saying istirjāʿ after a calamity earns the reward given on the day it occurred.
TABRISI:2:156-157/r13.anchor: من أصيب بمصيبة فأحدث استرجاعا وإن تقادم عهدها كتب الله له

TABRISI:2:156-157#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:156-157#2/r1.speaker: النبي
TABRISI:2:156-157#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṣādiq transmits from his forefathers, from the Prophet, that four traits qualify a person for Paradise: professing God's oneness, thanking Him for a blessing, seeking forgiveness after sin, and saying the istirjāʿ formula after calamity.
TABRISI:2:156-157#2/r1.anchor: وروى الصادق عليه السلام عن آبائه عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r1.claim: One grammatical analysis makes alladhina the subject and the following phrase in 2:157 its predicate.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r1.anchor: من الناس من يجعل {الذين} مبتدأ، وخبره قوله: {أولئك عليهم}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r2.claim: Another grammatical analysis makes alladhina an adjective describing the patient.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r3.claim: Al-Farra cites poetry using the related verbal nouns musab and musaba for a calamity that befalls someone.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r3.anchor:
أنشد الفراء:
فلو أنا بكينا من مصاب ... على حدث بكينا سيدينا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r4.claim: A musiba is an affliction that strikes; the word is not used for something that brings good fortune.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r4.anchor: ومعنى المصيبة: هي التي تصيب بالنكبة، ولا يقال فيما يصيب بخير: مصيبة (¬2)،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r5.claim: The y in musiba replaces a root waw and occupies the root's middle radical position.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r5.anchor: وياؤها منقلبة عن واو، هي عين الفعل.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r6.speaker: سيبويه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r6.claim: Sibawayh calls the hamza in the plural masaib an error: some speakers mistook the word's pattern and treated its root y as a long-vowel y; others say masawib, retaining the original form by analogy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r6.anchor: فحكى سيبويه: أن بعضهم قال في جمع مصيبة: مصائب فهمز، وهو غلط، وإنما هو مفعلة فتوهموها فعيلة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r7.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r7.claim: Abu Ali explains Sibawayh's analogy: speakers mistook the root y, which derives from waw, for a lengthening y like those in safina and sahifa, yielding safain and sahaif.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r7.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: قول سيبويه: وتوهموها فعيلة، أي: توهموا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r8.speaker: أبو الحسن
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r8.claim: Abu al-Hasan treats masilan for the plural of masil as the same kind of error: speakers took a root y for a lengthening y and formed the plural on the pattern of qadayd and qadbān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r8.anchor: ومثل هذا مما حمله أبو الحسن على الغلط: قول بعضهم في جمع مسيل: مسلان

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r9.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r9.claim: Abu Ishaq proposes that the hamza in masaib replaces a kasra waw, as in the word isada.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r9.anchor: وعند أبي إسحاق: الهمزة في مصائب بدل من الواو المكسورة على حد إبدالها في إسادة (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r10.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r10.claim: Abu Ali rejects Abu Ishaq's substitution theory: a noninitial kasra waw is not known to change this way, and the proposal lacks a comparable example.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r10.anchor: قال أبو علي: وليس القول عندي كذلك؛ لأن المكسورة غير أول لا تبدل كالمفتوحة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r11.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r11.claim: Abu Ali prefers the grammarians' account of mistaken analogy because it has more parallels; Abu Ishaq's substitution account is an unsupported assertion.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p427#2/r11.anchor: قال أبو علي: وليس القول عندي كذلك؛ لأن المكسورة غير أول لا تبدل كالمفتوحة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r1.claim: We and our possessions belong to God, and we are servants whom He may dispose of as He wills; the phrase acknowledges servitude, while the following words affirm resurrection.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r1.anchor: أي: نحن وأموالنا لله، ونحن عبيد يصنع بنا ما يشاء، وفي {إنا لله} إقرار له بالعبودية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r2.claim: Returning to God means returning to His sole rule: He temporarily gave people some power to benefit or harm, then that delegated control ends and rule returns to Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r2.anchor: ومعنى الرجوع إلى الله: الرجوع إلى انفراده بالحكم، كما كان أول مرة، إذ قد ملك قوما في الدنيا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r3.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq reads the first clause as confession of God's ownership and the second as confession that people will perish.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r3.anchor: وقال أبو بكر الوراق: {إنا لله}: إقرار منا له بالملك {وإنا إليه راجعون}: إقرار على أنفسنا بالهلك (¬4)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r4.speaker: النبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r4.claim: The author says the rewarded patience is shown by responding immediately to calamity without first lamenting, supported by the Prophet's saying that patience is at the first blow.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p430/r4.anchor: ما روي أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال لامرأة جزعت ثم راجعت: "إنما الصبر عند الصدمة الأولى" (¬5)

QASHANI:2:156-158/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:156-158/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:156-158/r1.claim: They see calamities as God's continual disposal of them and witness the effects of His power and the lights of His attributes' manifestations.
QASHANI:2:156-158/r1.anchor: من تصرفاتي فيهم دائما شاهدوا آثار قدرتي، بل أنوار تجليات صفتي

QASHANI:2:156-158/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:156-158/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:156-158/r2.claim: Saying that they belong to God means surrendering and knowing that they are His property, subject to His disposal.
QASHANI:2:156-158/r2.anchor: سلموا وأيقنوا أنهم ملكي، أتصرف فيه

QASHANI:2:156-158/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:156-158/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:156-158/r3.claim: Returning to God means effacing themselves in Him and witnessing their annihilation in Him.
QASHANI:2:156-158/r3.anchor: تفانوا في، وشاهدوا تهلكهم في بي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:156-158/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:156-158/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:156-158/r1.claim: Their words mean their property belongs to God and they are His servants, whom He may deal with as He wills.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:156-158/r1.anchor: { الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة } مما ذكر { قالوا إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون } أي: أموالنا لله، ونحن عبيدة يصنع بنا ما يشاء،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:156-158/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:156-158/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:156-158/r2.claim: God promises forgiveness for saying this in response to calamity.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:156-158/r2.anchor: ثم وعدهم على هذا القول المغفرة.

QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r12.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r12.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r12.claim: The patient meet affliction first with patience, then gratitude, then joy and pride.
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r12.anchor: قابلوا الأمر بالصبر لا بل بالشكر

QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r13.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r13.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r13.claim: Whoever sees created things as God’s property recognizes himself as a stranger to God’s judgment; the Creator has greater right over creation.

QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r14.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r14.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r14.claim: One who witnesses affliction recognizes the self as belonging to God and returning to Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r14.anchor: ومن شاهد المبلي علم أن ما يكون من الله

QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r15.claim: The one who is for God remains patient and standing, while the one who is by God loses choice and judgment, subsisting or vanishing as God wills.
QUSHAYRI:v1p78/r15.anchor: وشتان بين من كان لله وبين من كان بالله

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r4.claim: Verse 155 renews the call to patience, while 156 specifies patience integrated with faith and submission.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r4.anchor: 155. âyetin sonunda “Sabredenleri müjdele” buyurularak yeniden sabra vurgu yapılmış; 156. âyette bu sabrın imanla ve teslimiyetle bütünleşmiş bir sabır olduğu özellikle belirtilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r5.claim: The verses portray the first Muslims' firm faith, high morals, and strong morale, and define the exemplary believer through unshakable faith, trust, and surrender to God, awareness of belonging and returning to Him, hope in Him, and dignity before enemies.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r5.anchor: Bu yapının temel taşı Allah’a sarsılmaz iman, güven ve teslimiyettir; sadece Allah’a ait olduğumuzun ve en sonunda O’na döneceğimizin bilinci içinde

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r8.claim: These verses lavish praise on believers who patiently and steadfastly withstand life's hardships, especially while defending faith, homeland, and other high values, maintaining trust, surrender, optimism, and perseverance; God's own praise and affirmation of their guidance is the greatest honor.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:155/r8.anchor: Çünkü burada müminlere övgülerde bulunup onların hidayette olduklarını bildiren bizzat Allah’tır.

BAQILLANI:v1p145/r1.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p145/r1.speaker: علي بن أبى طالب
BAQILLANI:v1p145/r1.claim: Ali’s eulogy uses the istirjaʿ at a great loss, then affirms acceptance of God’s decree and submission to His command.
BAQILLANI:v1p145/r1.anchor: فإنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون رضينا عن الله قضاءه وسلمنا له أمره

BAQILLANI:v1p145/r2.author: al-Bāqillānī
BAQILLANI:v1p145/r2.speaker: author
BAQILLANI:v1p145/r2.claim: The listeners remained silent until the speech ended, then wept so loudly that their voices rose.
BAQILLANI:v1p145/r2.anchor: وسكت الناس حتى انقضى كلامه ثم بكوا حتى علت أصواتهم

BURHAN:v3p116/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p116/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p116/r6.claim: Iqtitāʿ is retaining one letter of a word while dropping the rest; al-Zarkashī rejects the claim that this device never occurs in the Qurʾān.
BURHAN:v3p116/r6.anchor: الاقتطاع وهو ذكر حرف من الكلمة وإسقاط الباقي

BURHAN:v3p116/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p116/r7.speaker: صاحب المثل السائر
BURHAN:v3p116/r7.claim: The author of al-Mathal al-sāʾir denies that this kind of truncation occurs in the Qurʾān, a claim al-Zarkashī rejects.
BURHAN:v3p116/r7.anchor: صاحب المثل السائر 1 ورود هذا النوع في القرآن العظيم

BURHAN:v3p116/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p116/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v3p116/r8.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās treats the disconnected letters as abbreviations for divine names: alif-lām-mīm means أنا الله أعلم وأرى, and alif-lām-mīm-ṣād means أنا الله أعلم وأفصل.
BURHAN:v3p116/r8.anchor: كما روى ابن عباس الم معناه أنا الله أعلم وأرى

BURHAN:v3p116/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p116/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p116/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the oath form من الله derives from أيمن, with its nūn deleted.
BURHAN:v3p116/r10.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في قوله من الله في القسم إنها ايمن التي تستعمل

SULAMI:v1p70/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p70/r1.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p70/r1.claim: Al-Qasim reads the declaration as calling the afflicted to accept God's allotment and patiently bear trial.
SULAMI:v1p70/r1.anchor: قال القاسم : هذه إشارة تدعو إلى الرضا بالقسمة والصبر على المحنة

SULAMI:v1p70/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p70/r2.speaker: القاسم
SULAMI:v1p70/r2.claim: Al-Qasim says every ordeal conceals blessing and the lights of blessing conceal the fires of love; he praises acceptance of events that neither piety nor disobedience can reverse.
SULAMI:v1p70/r2.anchor: قال القاسم : هذه إشارة تدعو إلى الرضا بالقسمة والصبر على المحنة . قال : تحت كل محنة نعمة وتحت كل أنوار النعمة نيران المحبة

ITQAN:v1p114/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p114/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p114/r6.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says his community alone among nations was given the response to calamity, إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون.
ITQAN:v1p114/r6.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني عن ابن عباس مرفوعا أعطيت أمتي شيئا لم يعطه أحد من الأمم عند المصيبة

ITQAN:v1p161/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p161/r1.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p161/r1.claim: Ibn Hajar calls a report weak because its chain is interrupted; if sound, its gathering means memorizing the Qur'an, while the earlier report from Abd Khayr is stronger and relied upon.
ITQAN:v1p161/r1.anchor: قال ابن حجر هذا الأثر ضعيف لانقطاعه وبتقدير صحته فمراده بجمعه حفظه في صدره

ITQAN:v1p161/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p161/r2.speaker: عكرمة
ITQAN:v1p161/r2.claim: Ikrima reports that after Abu Bakr's pledge, Ali explained that he stayed home to collect the Qur'an, fearing additions; Abu Bakr approved, and Ali had vowed not to wear his cloak except for prayer until it was gathered.
ITQAN:v1p161/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة قال لما كان بعد بيعة أبي بكر قعد علي بن أبي طالب في بيته فقيل لأبي بكر قد كره بيعتك

ITQAN:v1p161/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p161/r3.speaker: عكرمة
ITQAN:v1p161/r3.claim: Asked to arrange it in its revealed order, Ikrima says that even humans and jinn together could not produce that compilation.
ITQAN:v1p161/r3.anchor: فقلت لعكرمة الفوه كما أنزل الأول فالأول قال لو اجتمعت الإنس والجن على أن يؤلفوه ذلك التأليف ما استطاعوا

ITQAN:v1p161/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p161/r4.speaker: محمد بن سيرين
ITQAN:v1p161/r4.claim: Another report says Ibn Sirin's copy contained abrogating and abrogated material; he sought the manuscript but could not obtain it in Medina.
ITQAN:v1p161/r4.anchor: وفيه أنه كتب في مصحفه الناسخ والمنسوخ وأن ابن سيرين قال فطلبت ذلك الكتاب وكتبت فيه إلى المدينة فلم أقدر عليه

ITQAN:v1p161/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p161/r5.speaker: الحسن
ITQAN:v1p161/r5.claim: Al-Hasan reports that Umar ordered the Qur'an collected after learning that a verse had been with someone killed at Yamama; the chain is disconnected, and al-Suyuti explains Umar was the first to propose collection.
ITQAN:v1p161/r5.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي داود من طريق الحسن أن عمر سأل عن آية من كتاب الله فقيل كانت مع فلان قتل يوم اليمامة

ITQAN:v1p161/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p161/r6.speaker: ابن بريدة
ITQAN:v1p161/r6.claim: A disconnected report names Salim, freedman of Abu Hudhayfa, as the first collector; it says the name mushaf was chosen over the Jewish term sifr, and al-Suyuti treats Salim as one of those gathering at Abu Bakr's order.
ITQAN:v1p161/r6.anchor: من طريق كهمس عن ابن بريدة قال أول من جمع القرآن في مصحف سالم مولى أبي حذيفة

ITQAN:v1p161/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p161/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p161/r7.claim: Umar required two witnesses for material brought from the Prophet; al-Suyuti infers that Zayd required witnesses to confirm oral reception even when a written copy existed, as extra care.
ITQAN:v1p161/r7.anchor: وكان لا يقبل من أحد شيئا حتى يشهد شهيدان وهذا يدل على أن زيدا كان لا يكتفي لمجرد وجدانه مكتوبا

ITQAN:v1p245/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p245/r1.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p245/r1.claim: Ibn al-Jazari counts twelve causes of imala, including an earlier or later kasra or ya, whether adjacent, separated, inherent, estimated, or arising only in some forms of a word.
ITQAN:v1p245/r1.anchor: وأما الياء السابقة فأما ملاصقة للألف كالحياة والأيامى أو مفصولة بحرفين أحدهما الهاء كيدها

ITQAN:v1p245/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p245/r2.speaker: الكسائي
ITQAN:v1p245/r2.claim: Al-Kisa'i imala-reads the alif after ن in إنا and لله because the following alif in لله is imala-affected, but does not imala-read وإنا إليه because no such trigger follows.
ITQAN:v1p245/r2.anchor: وأما الإمالة لأجل الإمالة فكإمالة الكسائي الألف بعد النون من ﴿ إنا ﴾ ﴿ لله ﴾

ITQAN:v1p245/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p245/r3.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p245/r3.claim: Resemblance can cause imala: the feminine alif and the alifs in Musa and Isa resemble the alif in al-huda.
ITQAN:v1p245/r3.anchor: وأما الإمالة لأجل الشبه فإمالة ألف التأنيث في نحو الحسنى وألف موسى وعيسى لشبهها بألف الهدى

ITQAN:v1p245/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p245/r4.speaker: صاحب المبهج
ITQAN:v1p245/r4.claim: Frequent use is another cause; the author of al-Mubhij reports imala of الناس in all three case forms.
ITQAN:v1p245/r4.anchor: وأما الإمالة لكثرة الاستعمال فكإمالة الناس في الأحوال الثلاث على ما رواه صاحب المبهج

ITQAN:v1p245/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p245/r5.speaker: سيبويه
ITQAN:v1p245/r5.claim: Imala can distinguish a noun from a particle: Sibawayh says alphabetic bāʾ and tāʾ are names for spoken letters, unlike particles such as ma and wa.
ITQAN:v1p245/r5.anchor: وأما الإمالة للفرق بين الاسم والحرف فكإمالة الفواتح كما قال سيبويه إن إمالة باء وتاء في حروف المعجم لأنها أسماء

ITQAN:v1p245/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p245/r6.speaker: ابن الجزري
ITQAN:v1p245/r6.claim: The various imala grounds reduce to four forms and two principles, resemblance and indication; resemblance keeps articulation and neighboring sound aligned with the cause of imala.
ITQAN:v1p245/r6.anchor: وأما وجوهها فأربعة ترجع إلى الأسباب المذكورة أصلها اثنان المناسبة والإشعار

FARRA:v1p93/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p93/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p93/r6.claim: Arabs use kasra in inna specifically in the grief formula inna li-llāh; elsewhere before li they open it, as in ‘we love Zayd.’
FARRA:v1p93/r6.anchor: لم تكسر العرب (إنا) إلا في هذا الموضع مع اللام في التوجع خاصة.

FARRA:v1p93/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p93/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p93/r7.claim: Frequent use makes inna li-llāh function like one word, so the nūn takes kasra by the following lām, as in kāfir and al-ḥamdu li-llāh.
FARRA:v1p93/r7.anchor: وإنما كسرت فى «إنا لله» لأنها استعملت فصارت كالحرف الواحد

SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r1.claim: The preferred parse makes alladhīna an accusative adjective qualifying al-ṣābirīn.
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة }: فيه أربعة أوجه، أحدها: أن يكون منصوبا على النعت للصابرين،

SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r2.claim: Alternatively, alladhīna is accusative by way of praise.
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r2.anchor: الثاني: أن يكون منصوبا على المدح.

SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r3.claim: A nominative parse supplies an omitted subject, hum alladhīna; it may be a cut-off construction or a fresh resumption.
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r3.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون مرفوعا على خبر مبتدأ محذوف، أي: هم الذين،

SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r4.claim: Alladhīna may instead be the subject, with the conditional clause as its relative clause and the following أولئك عليهم صلوات as its predicate.
SAMIN-DURR:2:156/r4.anchor: الرابع: أن يكون مبتدأ، والجملة الشرطية من " إذا " وجوابها صلته، وخبره ما بعده

ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r3.claim: Trials make the companions' steadfastness persuasive to later people and contemporaries: endurance shows that truth and proof were clear; God grants the afflicted what benefits them in this life and the next.
ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r3.anchor: لأنهم يعلمون أنه لا يصبر على هذه الأشياء إلا من قد وضح له الحق وبان له البرهان

ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r4.claim: The saying means that the people and their property belong to God, are His servants, and He may do with them as He wills; this contains benefit and good for them.
ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r4.anchor: أي نحن وأموالنا لله ونحن عبيده يصنع بنا ما شاء، وفي ذلك صلاح لنا وخير.

ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r5.claim: Returning to God means affirming resurrection and reward for belief and for patience under trial.
ZAJJAJ:v1p230/r5.anchor: أي نحن مصدقون بأنا نبعث ونعطي الثواب على تصديقنا، والصبر على ما ابتلانا به.

NASHR:v2p33/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p33/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p33/r1.claim: Imāla may be caused by a following kasra, even an inflectional one, or by a following yāʾ, as with abid and mubayi'.
NASHR:v2p33/r1.anchor: وقد تكون الكسرة عارضة نحو من الناس

NASHR:v2p33/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p33/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p33/r2.claim: Imāla can reflect an underlying kasra: khafa derives from khawf, whose wāw became alif after moving with a preceding fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p33/r2.anchor: وأما الإمالة لأجل الكسرة المقدرة في المحل الممال فنحو: خاف. أصله: خوف بكسر عين الكلمة

NASHR:v2p33/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p33/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p33/r3.claim: Imāla can reflect an underlying yāʾ, as in yakhsha, al-huda, ata and al-thara, where a vocalized yāʾ became alif after fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p33/r3.anchor: وأما الإمالة لأجل الياء المقدرة في المحل الممال فنحو: يخشى، والهدى، وأتى، والثرى

NASHR:v2p33/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p33/r4.speaker: سيبويه
NASHR:v2p33/r4.claim: Sibawayh explains imāla in ṭāba, jā'a, shā'a and zāda by kasra arising with first- or second-person and feminine-plural forms; Ibn al-Jazari notes a possible qualification about final alifs.
NASHR:v2p33/r4.anchor: وهذا قول سيبويه ويمكن أن يقال: إن الإمالة فيه ليست بسبب أن الألف منقلبة عن ياء

NASHR:v2p33/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p33/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p33/r5.claim: Imāla in tala and ghaza follows yāʾ arising in their passive forms, although the active alifs derive from wāw.
NASHR:v2p33/r5.anchor: وأما الإمالة لأجل ياء تعرض في بعض الأحوال فنحو: تلا وغزا

NASHR:v2p33/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p33/r6.speaker: قتيبة عن الكسائي
NASHR:v2p33/r6.claim: Some explain imāla of rhyme words such as al-duha and tala-ha by nearby verse endings; Qutayba from al-Kisa'i tilts the alif in inna lillah due to Allah, but not in wa-inna ilayhi raji'un.
NASHR:v2p33/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك إمالة قتيبة عن الكسائي الألف بعد النون من: إنا لله لإمالة الألف من الله

NASHR:v2p33/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p33/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p33/r7.claim: Resemblance can cause imāla in feminine and augmentative alifs, as in al-husna and arta; Musa and Isa are also aligned with the feminine alif pattern.
NASHR:v2p33/r7.anchor: وأما الإمالة لأجل الشبه فإمالة ألف التأنيث في نحو الحسنى وألف الإلحاق في نحو: أرطى

NASHR:v2p33/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p33/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p33/r8.claim: Frequent use is another cause of imāla; he cites al-Hajjaj when used as a proper name.
NASHR:v2p33/r8.anchor: وأما الإمالة لأجل كثرة الاستعمال فكإمالتهم الحجاج علما لكثرته

ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r1.claim: The description signals that reward belongs to those who remain patient when the affliction first strikes, as the report says patience is at the first shock.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r1.anchor: إشارة إلى أن الأجر لمن صبر وقت إصابتها كما في الخبر إنما الصبر عند أول صدمة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r2.claim: A misfortune includes every unpleasant harm to a person, property, or family, great or small—even a thorn, mosquito bite, broken sandal strap, or extinguished lamp.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r2.anchor: والمصيبة تعم ما يصيب الإنسان من مكروه في نفس أو مال

ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r3.speaker: النبي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r3.claim: The Prophet sought God's protection and reward after even minor harms, and said that anything painful to a believer is a misfortune bringing reward.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r3.anchor: استرجع النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم من ذلك وقال : كل ما يؤذي المؤمن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r4.claim: Patience is not merely verbal istirja: the heart also recalls its purpose of knowing God and perfecting the self, return to the Lord and eternal life, departure from this fleeting world, and God's greater blessings, then submits.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r4.anchor: وليس الصبر بالاسترجاع باللسان بل الصبر باللسان وبالقلب بأن يخطر بباله ما خلق لأجله من معرفة الله تعالى وتكميل نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r5.claim: Patience is distinctive to human beings because reason and desire contend within them.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r5.anchor: والصبر من خواص الإنسان لأنه يتعارض فيه العقل والشهوة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r6.claim: Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh report from Ibn Abbas that the Prophet said this community received a response to misfortune unavailable to other nations: “We belong to God, and to Him we return.”
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r7.claim: A second report says earlier prophets did not receive this response; had Jacob received it, he would have said it when grieving for Joseph.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r8.speaker: أم سلمة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r8.claim: It is recommended after istirja to ask God to reward one in the affliction and replace it with something better; Muslim reports Umm Salama followed the Prophet's instruction after Abu Salama died and was given the Prophet as a better replacement.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r8.anchor: عن أم سلمة قالت : سمت رسول الله صلى الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r9.claim: The object of “give glad tidings” is omitted; it means glad tidings of immense mercy and abundant beneficence.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p23/r9.anchor: ومفعول ( بشر ) محذوف أي برحمة عظيمة وإحسان جزيل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.claim: “We belong to God” means that we are His servants and property.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r2.anchor: {الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة قالوا إنا لله} عبيدا وملكا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r3.claim: “To Him we return” means that we return in the Hereafter.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.speaker: أم سلمة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.claim: Umm Salama reports the Prophet's instruction to ask God for reward in one's calamity and a better replacement; God granted this to her after Abū Salama died, replacing him with the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r4.anchor: عن أم سلمة زوج النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنها قالت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says this community alone received the words of istirjāʿ for calamity; if anyone else had received them it would have been Jacob, who said “Alas for Joseph” at 12:84.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p169#2/r5.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير: ما أعطي أحد في المصيبة ما أعطي هذه الأمة يعني الاسترجاع ولو أعطيها أحد لأعطيها يعقوب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r1.speaker: النبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r1.claim: The Prophet promises that one who masters the Qur'an and acts by it will have parents crowned on Judgment Day with light brighter than the sun in a worldly house; no grading is stated.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r1.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال: " من قرأ القرآن فأحكمه وعمل بما فيه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r2.speaker: عمران بن حصين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r2.claim: When ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn sees a man reciting Qur'an to people and asking them for money, he says the verse's return formula and recalls the Prophet's warning to ask God through Qur'an, since some will recite it to solicit from people.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r2.anchor: عن رجل أن عمران بن حصين مر على رجل يقرأ على قوم فلما قرأ سأل فقال عمران: إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r3.claim: Baghawī notes al-Tirmidhī's version traces the report through al-Ḥasan from ʿImrān ibn Ḥuṣayn, and al-Bukhārī clarifies this is Khaythama al-Baṣrī, not Khaythama ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p43/r3.anchor: وقال محمد بن إسماعيل هو خيثمة البصري الذي روى عنه جابر الجعفي

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r1.claim: The address is directed either to the Messenger or to anyone capable of conveying good news.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r1.anchor: الخطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، أو لمن تتأتى منه البشارة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r2.claim: The object of “give glad tidings” is omitted but understood from context.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r3.claim: A calamity includes anything harmful that befalls a person.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r3.anchor: والمصيبة تعم ما يصيب الإنسان من مكروه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r4.claim: The Prophet said that everything which hurts a believer is a calamity for that believer.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r4.anchor: لقوله عليه الصلاة والسلام: «كل شيء يؤذي المؤمن فهو له مصيبة»

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r5.claim: Patience is not merely saying the return formula: it includes inwardly recognizing life’s purpose and return to God, recalling that remaining blessings far exceed what was taken, and submitting.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:156/r5.anchor: وليس الصبر بالاسترجاع باللسان، بل به وبالقلب بأن يتصور ما خلق لأجله، وأنه راجع إلى ربه، ويتذكر نعم الله عليه ليرى أن ما بقي عليه أضعاف ما استرده منه فيهون على نفسه، ويستسلم له

BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r1.claim: Biqai contrasts patience grounded in God, which earns divine companionship, with lesser patience that receives glad tidings of safety and reward; worldly honor alone does not define this rank.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r1.anchor: فكان للصابر الأول الصحبة بقوله : { إن الله مع الصابرين }

BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r2.claim: Muṣība derives from iṣāba: something falling on its intended mark, whether it agrees with the soul’s desire or opposes it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r2.anchor: من الإصابة وهو وقوع المسدد على حد ما سدد له من موافق لغرض النفس أو مخالف لها

BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r3.claim: The indefinite, feminine wording makes the promise cover any calamity, even a slight one.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r3.anchor: والمراد أي مصيبة كانت ولو قلت وضعفت بما أفهمه تأنيثه الفعل

BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r4.claim: The afflicted confess that God owns and encompasses all things and surrender themselves to their Lord, trusting that what He wills in this and every matter is best for them.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r4.anchor: أي الملك المحيط بكل شيء إسلاما بأنفسهم لربهم فهو يفعل بنا من هذه المصيبة وغيرها ما يريد

BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r5.claim: All affairs return to God alone; the phrase also affirms resurrection, when their return and accounting will become fully manifest.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r5.anchor: أي لا إلى غيره { راجعون } معنى في أن جميع أمورنا لا يكون شيء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says that surrendering losses to God and remembering return turns the loss of selves and property into stored provision with Him, a sign of faith and hope of meeting Him, and self-struggle in place of missed struggle in His path.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r6.anchor: قال الحرالي : لتكون ذلك غاية في إسلام ثمراتهم وأموالهم وما نقصوا من أنفسهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r7.claim: The formula applies universally: whoever says it after any calamity earns reward and is guided by God toward what the person had fallen short of.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p281/r7.anchor: وجعلها جامعة مطلقة لكل من أصابته مصيبة فاسترجع بها ثبت أجره

DURR-FULL:v1p376/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says earthly life is a place of trial and God commands patience; those who submit and say the return formula at calamity receive prayer, mercy, and guidance.
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ولنبلونكم} الآية قال: أخبر الله المؤمنين أن الدنيا دار بلاء وأنه مبتليهم فيها وأمرهم بالصبر

DURR-FULL:v1p376/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r2.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r2.claim: The Prophet says whoever says the return formula at calamity will have the loss repaired, a good outcome, and a pleasing righteous replacement.
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r2.anchor: وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من استرجع عند المصيبة جبر الله مصيبته وأحسن عقباه وجعل له خلفا صالحا يرضاه

DURR-FULL:v1p376/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r4.speaker: الضحاك
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r4.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says the verse applies to anyone who observes piety and fulfills the obligations.
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r4.anchor: عن جويبر قال: كتب رجل إلى الضحاك يسأله عن هذه الآية {إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون} أخاصة هي أم عامة فقال: هي لمن أخذ بالتقوى وأدى الفرائض

DURR-FULL:v1p376/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r5.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says the test concerns believers; patience is holding to God’s commands through calamities with Paradise promised, ṣalawāt means forgiveness, mercy includes safety from punishment, and the guided are those led by the return formula.
DURR-FULL:v1p376/r5.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله {ولنبلونكم} قال: ولنبتليكم يعني المؤمنين {وبشر الصابرين} قال: على أمر الله في المصائب يعني بشرهم بالجنة

DURR-FULL:v1p377/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r3.speaker: رسول الله
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r3.claim: The Prophet says this community received a privilege other peoples lacked: saying the return formula at calamity.
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم اعطيت أمتي شيئا لم يعطه أحد من الأمم أن يقولوا عند المصيبة

DURR-FULL:v1p377/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r4.claim: Saʿīd b. Jubayr says this community alone received the return formula at calamity; had earlier prophets received it, Jacob would have used it over Joseph, whose grief he voiced as “يا أسفى على يوسف.”
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r4.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال: لقد أعطيت هذه الأمة عند المصيبة شيئا لم تعطه الأنبياء من قبلهم

DURR-FULL:v1p377/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
