DURR-FULL:v1p377/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r5.claim: Qatāda urges anyone able to secure God’s prayer, mercy, and guidance through calamity to do so, saying God faithfully grants what is justly owed to Him.

DURR-FULL:v1p377/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r7.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr reports four habits earn a house in Paradise: affirming God’s oneness, saying the return formula at calamity, praising God on receiving a gift, and seeking forgiveness after sin.
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r7.anchor: عن عبد الله ابن عمرو قال: أربع من كن فيه بنى الله له بيتا في الجنة: من كان عصمة أمره لا إله إلا الله

DURR-FULL:v1p377/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r8.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r8.claim: ʿAlī reports that whoever bears a calamity patiently with good consolation receives three hundred ranks, each separated by the distance between heaven and earth.
DURR-FULL:v1p377/r8.anchor: عن علي قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم من صبر على المصيبة حتى يردها بحسن عزائها كتب الله له ثلثمائة درجة

DURR-FULL:v1p383/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p383/r1.speaker: ابن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v1p383/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAmr reports that when a believer loses a beloved person and bears the loss patiently in hope of reward, God promises Paradise.
DURR-FULL:v1p383/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمرو قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إن الله لا يرضى لعبده المؤمن إذا ذهب بصفيه من أهل الأرض فصبر واحتسب بثواب من الجنة

DURR-FULL:v1p383/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p383/r2.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
DURR-FULL:v1p383/r2.claim: Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī reports that sound reason consists of knowledge of God, obedience to God, and patience for God; without these, a person has no reason.
DURR-FULL:v1p383/r2.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: قسم الله العقل على ثلاثة أجزاء فمن كن فيه فهو العاقل

DURR-FULL:v1p383/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p383/r3.speaker: مطرف بن عبد الله بن الشخير
DURR-FULL:v1p383/r3.claim: After his son died, Muṭarrif b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Shikhkhīr dressed well and said God promised three traits for two calamities, each dearer than the world; he would not surrender to grief.
DURR-FULL:v1p383/r3.anchor: عن مطوف بن عبد الله بن الشخير أنه مات ابنه عبد الله فخرج وهو مترجل في ثياب حسنة فقيل له في ذلك

IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says the believer who submits to God’s decree and says the return formula at calamity receives God’s blessing, mercy, and confirmation of guidance.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : الذين اذا اصابتهم مصيبة قالوا انا لله وانا اليه راجعون قال : اخبر الله سبحانه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r2.speaker: النبي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r2.claim: The Prophet says whoever recites the return formula at calamity will have God mend the affliction, improve its outcome, and grant a pleasing righteous replacement.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r2.anchor: وقال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم : من استرجع عند المصيبة جبر الله مصيبته واحسن عقباه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r3.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says this community received a calamity formula withheld from earlier prophets; had Jacob received it, he would have used it when grieving Joseph.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r3.anchor: سمعت سعيد بن جبير يقول : لقد اعطيت هذه الامة عند المصيبة مالم تعط الانبياء قبلها : انا لله وانا اليه راجعون

IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r4.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak says the promise is for those who believe in piety and fulfill the obligations.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r4.anchor: عن الضحاك قال كتب اليه رجل يساله عن هذه الاية : الذين اذا اصابتهم مصيبة قالوا انا لله وانا اليه راجعون اخاصة هي ؟ أو عامة ؟ قال : هي لمن امن بالتقوى وادى الفرائض .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r5.speaker: عبد الصمد بن يزيد
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r5.claim: The servant’s formula means, “I belong to God, and I am returning to God.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p264#2/r5.anchor: ثنا عبد الصمد بن يزيد خادم الفضيل بن عياض يقول : قول العبد : انا لله وانا اليه راجعون تفسيرها : انى لله وانى إلى الله راجع .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r7.claim: The patient have the fullest patience because they understand that they belong to God, who may dispose of them as He wills, and that they will return to Him for reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r7.anchor: إذ يعلمون عند المصيبة أنهم ملك لله تعالى يتصرف فيهم كيف يشاء فلا يجزعون مما يأتيهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r8.claim: The formula counts only when it expresses sincere conviction; saying the words without belief earns no merit and is like empty noise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r8.anchor: فالمراد من القول هنا القول المطابق للاعتقاد إذ الكلام إنما وضع للصدق

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r9.claim: God taught this declaration as a motto at calamity because stating belief strengthens it by making it perceptible and publicly teaches it to others.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r9.anchor: لأن الاعتقاد يقوى بالتصريح لأن استحضار النفس للمدركات المعنوية ضعيف يحتاج إلى التقوية بشيء من الحس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r10.claim: The word calamity is discussed under 4:72.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p56/r10.anchor: والمصيبة يأتي الكلام عليها عند قوله تعالى : { فإن أصابتكم مصيبة قال قد أنعم الله علي } ( النساء : 72 )

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r1.claim: God informed the believers of coming trials so they could prepare to be patient and be less likely to despair.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه إنما أخبرهم بما سيصيبهم ليوطنوا أنفسهم على الصبر فيكون ذلك أبعد بهم من الجزع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r2.claim: Their words mean that they are God's servants and He may do with them as He wills.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r2.anchor: يريدون نحن عبيده يفعل بنا ما يشاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r3.claim: They affirm resurrection, reckoning for their deeds, and reward for their patience.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r3.anchor: يريدون نحن مقرون بالبعث والجزاء على أعمالنا والثواب على صبرنا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r4.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says this community received a formula for calamity unavailable to earlier prophets; he argues that if Jacob had received it, he would not have said “Alas for Joseph.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r4.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير لقد أعطيت هذه الامة عند المصيبة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r5.speaker: الفراء والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r5.claim: Al-Farra lists three Arabic forms, musiba, musaba, and musawba; al-Kisa'i says he heard a Bedouin say “May God mend your musawba.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p162#2/r5.anchor: قال الفراء وللعرب في المصيبة ثلاث لغات مصيبة ومصابة ومصوبة زعم الكسائي أنه سمع أعرابيا يقول جبر الله مصوبتك

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p467/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p467/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p467/r7.claim: The patient console themselves with this confession: they belong to God, who disposes of His servants as He wills, and return to Him in the afterlife, where not even an atom’s weight is lost; this acknowledges their servanthood and return.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p467/r7.anchor: أي: تسلوا بقولهم هذا عما أصابهم، وعلموا أنهم ملك لله يتصرف في عبيده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r1.claim: In Aḥmad’s report from Umm Salama, the Prophet promises that anyone struck by calamity who says the return formula and asks God to reward them and replace the loss with something better will receive that answer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r1.anchor: سمعت من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قولا سررت به

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r2.speaker: أم سلمة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r2.claim: Umm Salama reports that after Abū Salama died she made the prescribed supplication, doubting anyone could be better; after her waiting period the Prophet married her, addressed her concerns about jealousy, age, and dependents, and she regarded him as God’s better replacement.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r2.anchor: قالت أم سلمة: فحفظت ذلك منه، فلما توفي أبو سلمة استرجعت وقلت

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r3.claim: Muslim also transmits from Umm Salama the Prophet’s promise of divine reward and a better replacement for one who makes this supplication after calamity; she says it was fulfilled after Abū Salama’s death.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p468/r3.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم، عنها أنها قالت: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r1.claim: Al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī reports the Prophet’s promise that a Muslim who remembers an old calamity and renews the return formula receives anew the equivalent of the original reward; Aḥmad and Ibn Mājah transmit it, with variants in its chain wording.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r1.anchor: عن أبيها الحسين بن علي، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r2.claim: Abū Mūsā reports a divine saying: when a servant praises God and says the return formula after losing a child, God commands a house in Paradise called the House of Praise; al-Tirmidhī grades the report ḥasan gharīb.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r2.anchor: عن أبي موسى، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r3.speaker: الترمذي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r3.claim: Al-Tirmidhī calls the report about the House of Praise ḥasan gharīb and identifies Abū Sinān as ʿĪsā ibn Sinān.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p469/r3.anchor: وقال: حسن غريب. واسم أبي سنان: عيسى بن سنان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r1.speaker: أبوه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r1.claim: A report transmitted by Hishām from his father says Abū Bakr gathered the Qur’an after the Prophet; Ibn Kathir calls the report sound as well.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r1.anchor: عن هشام، عن أبيه، أن أبا بكر هو الذي جمع القرآن بعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r2.claim: After Qur’an reciters were killed in large numbers at Yamāma, ʿUmar urged Abū Bakr to collect the Qur’an lest it be lost as its memorizers died in battle; Abū Bakr hesitated, then agreed, as did Zayd.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r2.anchor: فلهذا أشار عمر على الصديق بأن يجمع القرآن؛ لئلا يذهب منه شيء بسبب موت من يكون يحفظه من الصحابة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r3.claim: At Yamāma, the Muslim army was initially shaken by the much larger force; about three thousand reciters regrouped, cried out to the Companions of al-Baqara, and fought until victory, though about five hundred reciters died.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r3.anchor: فكانوا قريبا من ثلاثة آلاف، ثم صدقوا الحملة، وقاتلوا قتالا شديدا، وجعلوا يتنادون: يا أصحاب سورة البقرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir calls this episode one of Zayd ibn Thābit’s greatest merits: Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and Zayd agreed to preserve the Qur’an in writing so it would not disappear with the deaths of memorizers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r4.anchor: وهذا المقام من أعظم فضائل زيد بن ثابت الأنصاري؛ ولهذا قال أبو بكر بن أبي داود

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r5.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that ʿUmar asked about a Qur’anic verse, learned that its bearer had been killed at Yamāma, and ordered the Qur’an gathered; the report calls this the first collection in a codex.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p25/r5.anchor: عن الحسن؛ أن عمر بن الخطاب سأل عن آية من كتاب الله فقيل: كانت مع فلان فقتل يوم اليمامة

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r1.speaker: الكسائي
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r1.claim: In some transmissions, al-Kisai uses imāla on the nūn of innā and lām of lillāh; other readers use tafkhīm.
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r1.anchor: أمال الكسائي في (مصيبة) في بعض الروايات النون من إنا ولام لله، والباقون بالتفخيم

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r2.speaker: الفراء والكسائي
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ and al-Kisai explain that imāla is allowed because kasra and frequent use make the phrase nearly one word; innā is not imālated before another name, since particles such as ḥattā and lākin resist it.
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r2.anchor: لا يجوز إمالة إنا مع غير اسم الله تعالى، وإنما وجب ذلك؛ لأن الأصل في الحروف وما يجري مجراها امتناع الإمالة

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r3.claim: Muṣība is severe harm to the self, named from iṣāba as though calamity strikes a person.
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r3.anchor: المصيبة: المضرة الشديدة على النفس، وأصلها من الإصابة، كأنه يصيبها بالنكبة

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r4.claim: Rujūʿ is a thing returning to its former state or ownership; Jishumi links it to 96:8.
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r4.anchor: والرجوع: مصير الشيء إلى ما كان، رجعت الدار إلى فلان إذا ملكها ثانيا، ومنه: (إن إلى ربك الرجعى (8)

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r8.claim: After mentioning the patient, the passage describes them: in loss of person or property they acknowledge being God's servants, property, and creation, and returning to His judgment at resurrection.
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r8.anchor: لما تقدم ذكر الصابرين عقب ذلك بوصفهم، فقال تعالى: الذين إذا أصابتهم مصيبة في النفس والمال

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r9.claim: Another account takes the return as arriving where no one but God has authority to judge.
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r9.anchor: وقيل: إلى حيث لا يملك الحكم سواه

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r10.claim: For a calamity from God, the duty is acceptance and belief in its goodness, wisdom, and benefit; for harm from people, one seeks God's redress and accepts His allowing it for a benefit.
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r10.anchor: فما كان من قبله، فالرضا به والاعتقاد لحسنه، وكونه حكمة ومصلحة، وما كان من غيره فيرجع إليه في الانتصاف

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r11.claim: The formula means God governs us as He wills in His own acts, and will secure justice for us as He wills when other people cause harm.
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r11.anchor: إنا لله يدبر فينا كيف شاء، وفي الثاني إنا له فينتصف لنا كما يشاء

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r12.claim: The acknowledgment implies acceptance: if God is one's Lord and His judgment is just and irresistible, despair has no point.
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r12.anchor: إذا أقر بأنه ربه وهو عدل حكمه، وأن ما يفعله فلا راد له، فلا فائدة في الجزع

JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r13.claim: The wording also intensifies acceptance, like telling someone struck by misfortune, 'I am yours.'
JISHUMI:v1p661#2/r13.anchor: أنه مبالغة في الرضا كما يقول لغيره إذا أصابه شيء: أنا لك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r3.claim: The patient receiving glad tidings are those who say the return formula at calamity, since it expresses surrender and acquiescence.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r3.anchor: المسترجعين عند البلاء لأن الاسترجاع تسليم وإذعان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r4.claim: The Prophet said whoever says the return formula at calamity will have it repaired, receive a good outcome, and be given a pleasing righteous replacement.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r4.anchor:
وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
70 ( من استرجع عند المصيبة جبر الله مصيبته وأحسن عقباه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r5.claim: When the Prophet’s lamp went out, he said the return formula and explained that anything harming a believer is a calamity for him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p232#3/r5.anchor:
وروي
71 أنه طفىء سراج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال ( إنا لله وإنا اليه راجعون )

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r10.claim: A calamity here befalls a person, family member, or property.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r10.anchor: يعني : إذا أصابتهم مصيبة في نفس أو أهل أو مال

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r11.claim: Their selves, families, and possessions belong to God, who does not wrong them in what He does.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r11.anchor: أي نفوسنا وأهلونا وأموالنا لله , لا يظلمنا فيما يصنعه بنا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r12.claim: Returning to God means resurrection, when He rewards the good-doer and punishes the wrongdoer.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p209/r12.anchor: يعني بالبعث في ثواب المحسن ومعاقبة المسيء

BURSEVI:v1p209/r14.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p209/r14.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p209/r14.claim: A calamity is anything painful that reaches a person; the Prophet is quoted as saying that anything which hurts a believer is a calamity for him, and the word derives from reaching its target.
BURSEVI:v1p209/r14.anchor: وأصلها الوصول من صاب السهم المرمي وأصابه وصل إليه

BURSEVI:v1p209/r15.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p209/r15.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p209/r15.claim: Saying ‘We belong to God’ confesses that people and their possessions are God's property; they should not grieve when He reclaims what is His, since He provides if they live and rewards them if they die.
BURSEVI:v1p209/r15.anchor: نحن عبيد الله والعبد وما في يده لمولاه فإن شاء أبقاه في أيدينا

BURSEVI:v1p209/r16.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p209/r16.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p209/r16.claim: What God gave is His favor, and taking it back stores it as a provision for the servant with Him; the formula acknowledges God's ownership.
BURSEVI:v1p209/r16.anchor: فما أعطانا ربنا كان فضلا منه ولا يليق بكرمه الارتجاع في عطاياه وإنما أخذه ليكون ذخيرة لنا عنده

BURSEVI:v1p209/r17.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p209/r17.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p209/r17.claim: The return formula confesses that people will perish and return to God.

BURSEVI:v1p209/r18.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p209/r18.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p209/r18.claim: Returning to God does not mean travel to a place or direction, which is impossible for God; it means reaching the Hereafter, where only God truly judges, unlike worldly appearances of human authority.
BURSEVI:v1p209/r18.anchor: ليس عبارة عن الانتقال إلى مكان وجهة فإن ذلك على الله محال بل المراد منه أن يصير إلى حيث لا يملك الحكم فيه سواه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r1.claim: A calamity is anything that hurts or befalls a believer; the source gives the related verbal forms.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { مصيبة } المصيبة: كل ما يؤذي المؤمن ويصيبه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r2.claim: Musiba is the singular of masa'ib; masuba, with a damma on sad, is another form, and musab can mean affliction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r2.anchor: والمصيبة واحدة المصائب. والمصوبة بضم الصاد مثل المصيبة.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r3.claim: Arabs unanimously hamza the plural masa'ib although its root has waw, by analogy with an added letter; the original plural is masa'ib without hamza.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r3.anchor: وأجمعت العرب على همز المصائب، وأصله الواو كأنهم شبهوا الأصلي بالزائد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r4.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r4.claim: The cited verse uses musab in a phrase about a man who brought greetings as an unjust tribute.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r4.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
أسليم إن مصابكم رجلا
أهدى السلام تحية ظلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r5.claim: The verb ṣāba, as in an arrow hitting paper, is a dialectal equivalent of aṣāba.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r5.anchor: وصاب السهم القرطاس يصيب صيبا لغة في أصابه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r6.claim: A calamity is a misfortune that befalls a person, even if slight, and the word is used for evil.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r6.anchor: والمصيبة: النكبة ينكبها الإنسان وإن صغرت وتستعمل في الشر

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r7.claim: A report attributed to Ikrima says the Prophet's lamp went out at night; he said the istirja, explaining that anything hurting a believer is a calamity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r7.anchor: روى عكرمة: أن مصباح رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم انطفأ ذات ليلة فقال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r8.speaker: أبو سعيد وأبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r8.claim: Muslim's report says illness, fatigue, sickness, sorrow, and even anxiety afflicting a believer expiate sins; al-Qurtubi says this confirms the prior report's meaning.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r8.anchor: خرج مسلم عن أبي سعيد وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنهما أنهما سمعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r9.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r9.claim: Ibn Majah transmits that whoever renews the istirja when recalling an old calamity receives the same reward as on the day it occurred.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r9.anchor: عن فاطمة بنت الحسين عن أبيها قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r10.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r10.claim: A report through Fitr ibn Khalifa and Ata ibn Abi Rabah says that when calamity strikes, one should remember the Prophet's calamity, the greatest of calamities.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r10.anchor: إذا أصاب أحدكم مصيبة فليذكر مصابه بي فإنها من أعظم المصائب

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r11.claim: Abu Umar affirms the Prophet's calamity is greater than every Muslim's later calamity: revelation ended, prophethood died, evil first appeared with Arab apostasy, and good began to diminish.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r11.anchor: قال أبو عمر: وصدق رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لأن المصيبة به أعظم من كل مصيبة يصاب بها المسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r12.speaker: أبو سعيد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r12.claim: Abu Sa'id said that before they had finished brushing the dust from the Prophet's grave, their hearts already felt changed.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157/r12.anchor: ما نفضنا أيدينا من التراب من قبر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r1.claim: The continuation of the poem cited from Abu al-Atahiya says calamities are universal and urges the sufferer to recall Muhammad and his calamity.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r1.anchor:
فإذا ذكرت محمدا ومصابه
فاذكر مصابك بالنبي محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r2.claim: God made these words a refuge for those afflicted and a protection for those tried because they gather blessed meanings.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r2.anchor: جعل الله تعالى هذه الكلمات ملجأ لذوي المصائب، وعصمة للممتحنين لما جمعت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r3.claim: The first phrase affirms God's oneness, servitude to Him, and His ownership.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r3.anchor: فإن قوله: «إنا لله» توحيد وإقرار بالعبودية والملك.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r4.claim: The second phrase acknowledges human mortality, resurrection from graves, and certainty that all affairs return to God, as they belong to Him.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r4.anchor: وقوله: { وإنآ إليه راجعون } إقرار بالهلك على أنفسنا والبعث من قبورنا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r5.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r5.claim: Said ibn Jubayr says these words were not given to any prophet before Muhammad; had Jacob known them, he would not have lamented Joseph.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r5.anchor: قال سعيد بن جبير رحمه الله تعالى: لم تعط هذه الكلمات نبيا قبل نبينا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r6.claim: Abu Musa's report says that when a servant's child dies, God asks what the parent said; if he praised God and said the istirja, God orders a heavenly house called the House of Praise.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r6.anchor: حدثني الضحاك عن أبي موسى أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r7.claim: Umm Salama reports the Prophet taught a supplication asking God for reward through calamity and a better replacement, which God grants to a Muslim who says it.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r7.anchor: روى مسلم عن أم سلمة قالت سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول:

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r8.claim: The Umm Salama report illustrates the glad tidings to the patient: God may provide a replacement, as He gave her the Prophet after Abu Salama died, or abundant reward, or both.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#2/r8.anchor: فهذا تنبيه على قوله تعالى: وبشر الصابرين

QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#3/r4.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#3/r4.claim: In Bukhari, Umar calls prayer and mercy the two equal portions, and guidance the additional topping.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:156-157#3/r4.anchor: وفي البخاري وقال عمر رضي الله عنه: نعم العدلان ونعم العلاوة:

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r1.claim: After commanding glad tidings to the patient in 2:155, the next verse explains how a person is patient and what that glad tiding entails.
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r1.anchor: لما قال : { وبشر الصابرين } ( البقرة : 155 ) بين في هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r2.claim: Afflictions may come from God or from human beings: fear may involve drowning, fire, or lightning from God, while the Arabs' united hostility toward the Prophet is a human cause.
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r2.anchor: الخوف الذي يكون من الله فمثل الخوف من الغرق والحرق والصاعقة وغيرها

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r3.claim: Hunger follows poverty, which may result from God destroying wealth or from people taking it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r3.anchor: وأما الجوع فلأجل الفقر ، وقد يكون الفقر من الله

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r4.claim: Loss of wealth comes from God through disasters striking property and crops, or from enemies whose pressure prevents people from tending their land.
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r4.anchor: ونقص الأموال من الله تعالى إنما يكون بالجوائح التي تصيب الأموال والثمرات ، ومن العدو

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r5.claim: Loss of life comes from God through death and from people through killing.
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r5.anchor: ونقص الأنفس من الله بالإماتة ومن العباد بالقتل

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r6.claim: Al-Qadi says the wording does not assign the affliction to God alone but covers harms caused by God or by people; both bring duties, and the servant must obey rather than abandon them.
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r6.anchor: قال القاضي : إنه تعالى لم يضف هذه المصيبة إلى نفسه بل عمم

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r7.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r7.claim: For a God-sent affliction, the servant should accept it as wise, just, good, and beneficial, submit to God's decree, and not give way to grief; God judges rightly (40:20).
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r7.anchor: فالذي يناله من قبله تعالى يجب أن يعتقد فيه أنه حكمة وصواب وعدل وخير وصلاح

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r8.claim: The formula acknowledges servitude and entrusts matters to God, expressing acceptance of his decree because he decrees only what is right.
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r8.anchor: لأن في إقرارهم بالعبودية تفويض الأمور إليه والرضا بقضائه

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r9.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r9.claim: When another person causes the affliction, the duty is to seek vindication from God, restrain anger, and avoid unlawful retaliation; the formula acknowledges God's command to keep within those limits.
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r9.anchor: أما إذا نزلت به المصيبة من غيره فتكليفه أن يرجع إلى الله تعالى في الانتصاف منه وأن يكظم غيظه وغضبه

RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r10.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r10.claim: The formula means God governs the servant's affairs as he wills when the harm comes from God, and will vindicate the servant as he wills when another person caused it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p139#3/r10.anchor: كأنه يقول في الأول ، إنا الله يدبر فينا كيف يشاء ، وفي الثاني يقول : إنا لله ينتصف لنا كيف يشاء

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r1.speaker: الكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r1.claim: In some transmissions al-Kisa'i uses imala on Ana and the lām of Allah, while other readers use tafkhim; the kasra and frequent use make imala possible, and al-Farra and al-Kisa'i disallow it for Ana with other names and for forms such as hatta and lakin.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r1.anchor: أمال الكسائي في بعض الروايات من { أنا } ولام { لله } والباقون بالتفخيم

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r2.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq reads 'we belong to God' as acknowledging God's ownership, and 'to him we return' as acknowledging our destruction.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر الوراق { إنا لله } إقرار منا له بالملك

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r3.claim: Return to God cannot mean movement to a place or direction, which is impossible for God.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r3.anchor: الرجوع إليه ليس عبارة عن الانتقال إلى مكان أو جهة

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r4.claim: Return means reaching the hereafter, where God alone holds judgment and no one else can apparently benefit or harm people; sovereignty's return likewise means power, not movement.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r4.anchor: بل المراد أنه يصير إلى حيث لا يملك الحكم فيه سواه

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r5.claim: This declaration affirms resurrection and that God will reward the patient according to their deserts without losing the good-doers' reward.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r5.anchor: هذا يدل على أن ذلك إقرار بالبعث والنشور

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r6.claim: The first clause expresses present acceptance of whatever affliction has come; the return clause expresses acceptance of what will come, including reward, entrusting affairs to God, and vindication against a wrongdoer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r6.anchor: يدل على كونه راضيا بكل ما نزل به في الحال من أنواع البلاء

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r7.claim: The return clause also expresses self-humbling and contentment with the afterlife reward God promised.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r7.anchor: فيكون مذللا نفسه ، راضيا بما وعده الله به من الأجر في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r8.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r8.claim: A prophetic report says that whoever says the return formula at a calamity will have the loss repaired, a good outcome, and a pleasing righteous replacement; Razi gives no grading.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r8.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r9.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r9.claim: When the Prophet's lamp went out he said the formula; when asked whether it was a calamity, he said that anything which harms a believer is a calamity. No grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r9.anchor: روي أنه طفيء سراج رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقال : ( إنا لله وإنا إليه راجعون )

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r10.speaker: أم سلمة
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r10.claim: Umm Salama says Abu Salama told her that the Prophet taught an afflicted Muslim to say the formula and ask God for recompense and a better replacement; after Abu Salama died she said it, and God replaced him with Muhammad. No grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r10.anchor: قالت أم سلمة : حدثني أبو سلمة أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( ما من مسلم يصاب بمصيبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas says that a believer who submits to God and says the formula at affliction receives three gifts: divine blessing, mercy, and confirmation on the path of guidance.
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس : أخبر الله أن المؤمن إذا سلم لأمر الله تعالى ورجع واسترجع عند مصيبته

RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r13.speaker: ابن مسعود
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r13.claim: Ibn Masud says falling from the sky would be preferable to saying about something God decreed, 'If only it had not happened.'
RAZI-FULL:v4p140/r13.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود : لأن أخر من السماء أحب إلى من أن أقول لشيء قضاه الله تعالى : ليته لم يكن

RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r5.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r5.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi distinguishes obligations—submit to God's command and decree and persist in duties despite worldly affliction—from the recommended public recitation of the formula, which others may imitate and which displays steadfastness to disbelievers.
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r5.anchor: قال أبو بكر الرازي : اشتملت الآية على حكمين : فرض ونفل

RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r6.speaker: داود الطائي
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r6.claim: Dawud al-Ta'i defines asceticism as not loving to remain in the world and says the best deed is contentment with God; a Muslim should not grieve, knowing every calamity carries reward.
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r6.anchor: وحكي عن داود الطائي قال : الزهد في الدنيا أن لا يحب البقاء فيها

RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r7.claim: Razi closes by describing contentment with God's decree through two paths, self-directed effort (tasarruf) and divine attraction (jadhb), then elaborates the first.
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r7.anchor: العبد إنما يصبر راضيا بقضاء الله تعالى بطريقن : إما بطريق التصرف ، أو بطريق الجذب

RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r8.claim: Through self-directed effort, attachment to an object makes it a source of affliction and turns the heart from created things toward the holy: Adam's attachment to the Garden led to its loss, leaving him with remembrance of God.
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r8.anchor: فإن آدم عليه السلام لما تعلق قلبه بالجنة جعلها محنة عليه حتى زالت الجنة

RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r9.claim: Jacob's comfort in Joseph was followed by separation, leaving Jacob with remembrance of God.
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r9.anchor: ولما استأنس يعقوب بيوسف عليهما السلام أوقع الفراق بينهما حتى بقي يعقوب مع ذكر الحق

RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r10.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r10.claim: Razi says Muhammad's hope for Meccan support was met with their becoming his fiercest opponents, and cites the Prophet's saying that no prophet was harmed as much as he was; no grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r10.anchor: ولما طمع محمد عليه السلام من أهل مكة في النصرة والإعانة صاروا من أشد الناس عليه حتى قال : ( ما أوذي نبي مثل ما أوذيت )

RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r11.claim: A second path removes the object entirely, leaving neither affliction nor favor, so the servant returns to God.
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r11.anchor: أن لا يجعل ذلك الشيء بلاء ولكن يرفعه من البين حتى لا يبقى لا البلاء ولا الرحمة

RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r12.claim: A third path is that God gives directly something better than what the servant expected, making the servant feel ashamed and return to God's mercy.
RAZI-FULL:v4p141/r12.anchor: أن العبد متى توقع من جانب شيئا أعطاه الله تعالى بلا واسطة خيرا من متوقعه فيستحي العبد فيرجع إلى باب رحمة الله
